name: Diginex Limited

profile.description: Diginex Limited provides sustainability RegTech software and advisory services, including the diginexESG reporting platform, diginexLUMEN supply-chain risk assessment, diginexAPPRISE worker-voice data collection, and diginexCLIMATE carbon accounting [6]. Since its January 2025 Nasdaq IPO the company has pursued an acquisition-led transformation (Plan A, Matter, The Remedy Project) and in April 2026 agreed an all-share deal valued at ~US$1.5B for customer-engagement AI company Resulticks, amended on August 14, 2026 with targeted completion of October 30, 2026 subject to shareholder, Nasdaq and regulatory approvals [3]. FY2026 (ended March 31, 2026) revenue was $3.6M against a net loss of $25.5M [1][6]. The share price has collapsed from a 52-week high of $196 (split-adjusted) to ~$1.40, a ~$70M market cap [6].

innovation.analysis: Track Record (1/3): Diginex has bolted on Plan A (European carbon accounting), Matter and The Remedy Project, lifting FY2026 revenue 77% to $3.6M, but growth is acquired rather than organic and the platform has not yet proven a new self-sustaining revenue stream [1][2]. AI Deployment (1/2): Management is repositioning toward an 'AI, data and sustainability platform' built around Resulticks' Genie agentic framework, but that deal was still pending at last disclosure and no AI-driven revenue or savings have been quantified [3][7]. Market Share (0/2): At $3.6M in revenue Diginex is a sub-scale participant in a crowded ESG-software market with no share data. Product Pipeline (1/2): Management targets ~$280M combined revenue by 2027 if Resulticks closes, but this is deal-dependent rather than a dated product roadmap [3]. R&D Intensity (0/1): No R&D expense is reported; FY2026 operating costs of $28.5M were overwhelmingly G&A [6].
innovation.label: WEAK

inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (2/4): The original diginex mission of making ESG and supply-chain labor data transparent (e.g., diginexAPPRISE gathering data directly from supply-chain workers on their working conditions) is clear and service-oriented, but the pivot toward a customer-engagement AI roll-up dilutes it [6][3]. Community Impact (0/2): No charitable program or community investment with specific amounts was found. Employee Retention (0/2): The CEO seat has turned over repeatedly — Plan A founder Lubomila Jordanova took over in January 2026 and Resulticks CEO Redickaa Subrammanian is slated to become CEO on completion — and no retention data exists [3][4]. Insider Buying (1/2): Management cites a $25M founder buy-in tied to the expansion push, but this is offset by reports of a large insider warrant sale and a warrant-term extension that raised dilution concerns, leaving the insider signal roughly balanced [3][5].
inspiration.label: WEAK

infrastructure.analysis: HARD RULE TRIGGERED — Liquidity Floor: three-month average volume of 612,708 shares × $1.40 = ~$0.86M per day, below IOWN's $1,000,000 threshold, so Infrastructure = 0 regardless of other metrics [6]. (FMP reports a higher longer-window average of ~1.77M shares, but recent sessions trade ~300K shares, so the yfinance figure is used.) For reference, the unfloored growth-sleeve calculation would be 5.4/10: D/E of 0.77% scores 1.0 (no interest-bearing debt), revenue growth of 3.3% (latest-quarter YoY per Yahoo; FY2026 was +77%) scores 0.78, the FY2022–FY2026 4-year revenue CAGR of 34.0% (derived from FMP statements; only five fiscal years exist) scores 1.0 at 2x weight, while ROE of -250% and a TTM net margin of -1,137% both score 0; forward P/E and PEG are not meaningful with negative earnings and are excluded [1][6].
infrastructure.label: WEAK

ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (3/9): EXPOSED. Diginex's core products — ESG report drafting, materiality assessment, data collection and carbon calculations — are document- and data-workflow software that general-purpose generative AI and large ERP/sustainability suites can increasingly automate; the company itself is seeking to buy AI capability (Resulticks) rather than defending an existing proprietary moat [3][7]. The worker-voice supply-chain data (APPRISE) is the most defensible asset, but it is a small revenue line. AI Opportunity (0/1): No quantified AI revenue is reported; the Resulticks AI revenue would only consolidate if and when the pending transaction closes [3].
ai_resilience.label: HIGH RISK

infinite_game.summary: Through Sinek's lens Diginex is playing a finite game: an acquisition-and-narrative roll-up whose identity has shifted from crypto (the predecessor Diginex/EQONEX), to ESG RegTech, to an AI customer-engagement platform within roughly two years. A $1.5B all-share deal for a company many times its size, rotating CEOs, warrant extensions and law-firm investigations into the deal valuation point to short-term financial engineering rather than a durable cause [3][4].

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (1/3): The supply-chain transparency mission (giving workers a voice on conditions) had genuine service orientation, but leadership now frames the company around scale and AI revenue targets (~$280M by 2027), and the cause has not been held through any test of time [3][6].

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (0/2): A 114-person organization absorbing several acquisitions, with the CEO role changing hands in January 2026 and again on the planned Resulticks close, provides no evidence of a stable circle of safety [3][4].

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): Company communications focus on deal scale and revenue targets; there is no evidence of management learning from or acknowledging stronger ESG-software competitors.

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): Diginex is undeniably willing to reinvent itself — from ESG reporting to a combined AI, data and sustainability platform — but the pivots look driven by capital-markets opportunity and a collapsing share price rather than by a Just Cause [3][7].

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (0/2): Rather than sacrificing near-term optics for long-term capability, leadership has pursued serial all-share acquisitions and warrant amendments that heavily dilute existing holders; FY2026 G&A nearly tripled to $28.5M while revenue was only $3.6M [2][4].

investment_thesis: The bull case rests on transformation: FY2026 revenue grew 77% to $3.6M with no interest-bearing debt, and if the Resulticks combination closes, management targets roughly $280M of combined revenue by 2027 from an AI-enabled customer-engagement and sustainability-data platform [1][3]. At ~$70M market cap and ~0.3x book, any successful integration would be a large re-rating from a depressed base [6].
thesis_continued: The bear case is severe. FY2026 net loss of $25.5M was roughly 7x revenue, TTM net margin is about -1,137%, ROE is -250%, and cash was only $4.9M at year-end, so the business depends on continued equity issuance [1][2][6]. The stock has fallen from a split-adjusted high of $196 to $1.40, law firms are reviewing the Resulticks valuation, and three-month average volume of ~613K shares (~$0.86M/day) breaches IOWN's $1M liquidity floor [4][6].
key_catalysts: Completion of the ~$1.5B all-share Resulticks combination (targeted October 30, 2026, subject to shareholder, Nasdaq and regulatory approval), which would consolidate an established AI customer-engagement revenue base [3]
Cross-selling Plan A carbon accounting and diginexLUMEN supply-chain tools into EU CSRD/CSDDD compliance demand as acquired businesses integrate [1][7]
Disclosure of FY2027 interim results showing whether acquired revenue is growing organically and whether G&A ($28.5M in FY2026) can be cut [2]
key_risks: Liquidity and financing: $4.9M of cash against a ~$25M annual net loss implies near-term dilution; average dollar volume of ~$0.86M/day fails IOWN's $1M liquidity floor [1][6]
Deal risk: the Resulticks transaction may not close, and law-firm investigations into the deal valuation plus a change of CEO on completion create governance and litigation overhang [3][4]
Core ESG-reporting software is exposed to AI automation and to regulatory rollback of ESG disclosure mandates, undermining the original product's demand [7]
